title: Woven wheel
subtitle: A raised circular motif woven over spokes for flower and button effects
excerpt: A woven wheel is a small circular motif built by first laying an odd number of straight spokes and then weaving the thread over and under the spokes in a spiral until the wheel is full. The finished wheel is raised and textured, resembling a small rose or a woven button.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), wheel and raised stitch chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Weldon's Practical Needlework, Vol. 2 (1886), woven circle entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: The straight foundation stitches laid in a wheel pattern before weaving. An odd number of spokes is required so the weaving alternates correctly as it spirals.

content.text: A woven wheel begins with a

of five or seven straight stitches radiating from a central point. The weaving thread then spirals outward, going over one spoke and under the next without entering the fabric, until the spokes are covered and the wheel is full.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Perle 8 or stranded cotton 3 strands; the weaving thread can be the same or contrasting

content.text: Work five straight stitches radiating from one central hole, evenly spaced around a circle of the desired finished size.
Bring the weaving thread up through the centre hole beside the spokes.
Slide the blunt needle over one spoke and under the next, working in a spiral outward from the centre.
Continue spiralling until the spokes are fully covered to their tips.
Take the needle down through the fabric at the edge of the last spoke and fasten off at the back.

items.fix: Always use an odd number of spokes (5 or 7). Odd numbers keep the over-under alternation cycling forward.
items.cause: An even number of spokes was used.
items.symptom: The weaving loses the over-under alternation

items.fix: Work the first few spiral rows with lighter tension, nudging them outward gently with the needle tip before adding the next row.
items.cause: Too much weaving thread packed at the centre before spreading outward.
items.symptom: The wheel is lumpy at the centre and flat at the edge

content.text: Woven wheels make quick, effective flower motifs and are often combined with
petals around them. The same spoke-and-weave principle gives the spider's web stitch its structure.
